column4: tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `interp alias {} g {} uplevel #0; proc ::p {} { g {set x 1} }; p` sets ::x to 1
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: setter with late `g` (uplevel #0) and `put` (set x) aliases sets ::x to 99
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `uplevel #0 {::inner {::set g 1}}` with ::inner aliased to `uplevel 0` sets ::g to 1
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: the same with ::inner aliased to `eval` sets ::g to 1
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `::n::setter` runs `uplevel #0 { eval { put 2 } }`; the global alias `put` (set x) wins over ::n::put, ::x is 2
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `uplevel #0 { eval { helper } }` from ::n::setter runs ::helper: global_hit exists, namespaced_hit does not (1 0)
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4 (and 9.0.4 cited in the test): `uplevel #0 [list set k 77]` sets ::k to 77
tclsh: `uplevel #0 [list puts hi]` writes no variable (TN); summary comes back opaque instead of empty
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `uplevel 1 { ::set n 1 }` sets the caller's n, not ::n (`list [info exists ::n] [c]` -> 0 1)
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4, argv empty: g stays `upvar #0`, `p` sets ::x to 1; the may-join of both bindings must keep x
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4, argv empty: `mutate g {}` is `list`, g survives, `p` sets ::x to 1
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `set _ [bind local]` with bind = `upvar #0 g` links local to ::g; `set local 1` sets ::g to 1

tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `interp alias {} ::n::g {} list` creates ::n, so `proc ::n::p` exists (info commands ::n::* -> ::n::p ::n::g); with ::n present `::n::p` sets ::x to 1. The analyser finds no ::n::p body
tclsh 8.6.18, 9.0.4: `rename set moved; interp alias {} put {} moved {café}; ... p` sets ::café to VALUE; summary is opaque and empty

tclsh 8.4.20, 8.6.18, 9.0.4, 9.1.0: `proc p {name} {upvar #0 {} $name; set ordinary VALUE}; p ordinary` sets the global named "" to VALUE (also experiments/name-handling/results/global-empty-alias-cell-20261014)
AGENTS.md registry rule: a registry entry replacing `global` with a VarWrite descriptor must drive the summary; names {} instead of {x}
